text:
What is not a difference
Push, fetch, branches, and review comments are Git plus a database row. A developer who learned chapters 8–11 does not relearn them here. The UI names a pull request; Gerrit (chapter 27) names a change. Under both, the bytes are still a branch on a remote.
Webhooks out of either lightweight forge are the same idea as GitLab’s: HTTP to your CI when a ref moves. Chapter 32 is that integration. This chapter does not stand up a runner.

title: Gitea vs Forgejo vs GitLab
section: How to read the license row
text:
How to read the license row
Pick Forgejo when the operator must be able to show that the forge itself stays free software, with a non-profit holding the name and no Enterprise fork of the same tree.
Pick Gitea when the MIT terms are a requirement (you need to ship a closed product derived from the forge) or you are already paying for Gitea Enterprise and the company build is the point.
Pick GitLab when the requirement is CI, a container registry, and security scanning inside one installer, and you can afford the machine that installer expects. A 2 GB lab VM is a Forgejo conversation. It is a bad GitLab conversation.
The next page is how the lightweight shape is deployed, and where SQLite stops being the right database.

title: Deployment and Scaling
text:
Deployment and Scaling
After this page you can sketch a Forgejo or Gitea layout and name the first limit you will hit.

title: Deployment and Scaling
section: One directory is the whole server
text:
One directory is the whole server
The container’s data directory holds the bare repositories, the database, and the config. On the standard image that directory is /data. SQLite, when you leave the database unset, is a file in that tree (gitea.db, including on Forgejo: the filename stayed). Config is app.ini under the same tree.
./data/                      (bind mount → /data)
  git/repositories/          bare repos
  gitea/gitea.db             SQLite, until you move it
  gitea/conf/app.ini         generated on first start
Environment variables of the form FORGEJO__section__KEY write app.ini for you. Gitea uses the same pattern with the prefix GITEA__. A value already stored in app.ini is not cleared by unsetting the variable. Edit the file, or start from an empty data directory.
Two images ship:








Image
Data mount
SSH inside the container




codeberg.org/forgejo/forgejo:15
/data
port 22


codeberg.org/forgejo/forgejo:15-rootless
/var/lib/gitea
port 2222



The lab uses the first. Rootless is the same product with a different mount and a different internal SSH port. Mirror data.forgejo.org when codeberg.org is not reachable from the build machine.

title: Deployment and Scaling
text:
Where it stops being small
SQLite has one writer. A desk, a class, or a company of tens of people is the design center. A busy public forge is not. The move is mechanical:

Keep Git bytes on local disk. NFS for the repository directory is a corruption risk unless you already know that filesystem’s locking story. Chapter 36 is the storage chapter.
Move the database to Postgres when SQLite lock time shows up in the logs. Set FORGEJO__database__DB_TYPE=postgres and a host. Do this before the file is large, and take a backup first (chapter 37).
Put LFS and package blobs on object storage when the data disk fills with artifacts, not when the Git packs do.
Scale CI by adding runners, not by cloning the Forgejo process. Actions are optional. The server is still one writer of its own database.

There is no supported active-active pair of Forgejo nodes over one SQLite file. High availability here means backups, a second disk, and a practiced restore. GitLab’s multi-node shape is a different product.

title: Deployment and Scaling
text:
Upgrades
Pin an image tag (:15 or :15.0), not latest. Moving from major N to N+1 is a manual upgrade with a backup of /data in front of it. Patch releases inside 15.0 replace the container and keep the directory.
Gitea’s image is docker.io/gitea/gitea:1.27. Same directory layout, same port story, GITEA__ environment names. Do not run both compose projects against one data directory.
The hands-on page brings Forgejo up, pushes desk-api, then shows the Gitea file as the same lab with the image line changed.

title: Hands-On: Gitea and Forgejo
text:
Hands-On: Gitea and Forgejo
Bring up Forgejo 15 on Linux, push desk-api, tear it down, then read the Gitea file as the same lab with one image line changed.
Examples were checked against the Forgejo 15 LTS docs and Gitea 1.27. You need Docker, or Podman with podman compose. The commands below say docker compose. On Podman, substitute podman compose. Do not point this lab at a Forgejo you already use.

title: Hands-On: Gitea and Forgejo
text:
Forgejo
Host port 3000 is HTTP. Host port 2222 is Git SSH, so the lab does not take the machine’s own sshd on port 22. If either host port is already taken, stop. Another forge is probably there.
mkdir -p ~/desk/forgejo-lab
cd ~/desk/forgejo-lab
mkdir -p data
cat > compose.yml <<'EOF'
services:
  server:
    image: codeberg.org/forgejo/forgejo:15
    environment:
      USER_UID: "1000"
      USER_GID: "1000"
      FORGEJO__server__DOMAIN: localhost
      FORGEJO__server__ROOT_URL: http://localhost:3000/
      FORGEJO__server__SSH_PORT: "2222"
      FORGEJO__server__HTTP_PORT: "3000"
    restart: unless-stopped
    volumes:
      - ./data:/data
    ports:
      - "3000:3000"
      - "2222:22"
EOF
docker compose up -d
docker compose ps
USER_UID should be your numeric id (id -u) if 1000 is not you, or the data directory will be owned by the wrong account. Wait until the HTTP port answers:
curl -fsS -o /dev/null -w '%{http_code}\n' http://127.0.0.1:3000/
A 200 or a 303 is enough. Open http://localhost:3000/ in a browser. The installation page asks for the administrator. Create that account. Leave the database on SQLite. Submit, then sign in.
Create a repository named desk-api. Empty is fine. The UI shows two clone URLs. The SSH one should contain :2222. If it says port 22, SSH_PORT did not land in app.ini and the compose environment block needs another look.

title: Hands-On: Gitea and Forgejo
text:
Push desk-api
~/desk/desk-api is the project from chapter 3. Add this forge as a second remote (chapter 11). Use the HTTP URL from the UI if you have not loaded an SSH key into the forge yet.
cd ~/desk/desk-api
git remote add forgejo http://127.0.0.1:3000/ADMIN/desk-api.git
git push -u forgejo main
Replace ADMIN with the username you just created. The password is the one from the installation page. After the push, the file list in the browser matches git log --oneline locally.
SSH, once the UI has your public key:
git remote set-url forgejo ssh://git@127.0.0.1:2222/ADMIN/desk-api.git

title: Hands-On: Gitea and Forgejo
text:
Tear it down
cd ~/desk/forgejo-lab
docker compose down
./data is still on disk. docker compose down does not delete that directory. Delete ~/desk/forgejo-lab when you are finished with the lab. Leave ~/desk/desk-api in place, and remove the remote if you do not want it:
cd ~/desk/desk-api
git remote remove forgejo

title: Hands-On: Gitea and Forgejo
text:
The Gitea file
Do not start this while the Forgejo container is still bound to 3000 and 2222. Same lab, other project:
mkdir -p ~/desk/gitea-lab/data
cd ~/desk/gitea-lab
cat > compose.yml <<'EOF'
services:
  server:
    image: docker.io/gitea/gitea:1.27
    environment:
      USER_UID: "1000"
      USER_GID: "1000"
      GITEA__server__DOMAIN: localhost
      GITEA__server__ROOT_URL: http://localhost:3000/
      GITEA__server__SSH_PORT: "2222"
      GITEA__server__HTTP_PORT: "3000"
    restart: unless-stopped
    volumes:
      - ./data:/data
    ports:
      - "3000:3000"
      - "2222:22"
EOF
docker compose up -d, the same installation page, a repository, a push, docker compose down. The screen is Gitea’s. The Git remote is still just a URL.

title: Hands-On: Gitea and Forgejo
text:
Done when

Forgejo’s UI showed desk-api after git push
the SSH clone URL contained port 2222
both compose projects are down, and ~/desk/desk-api still has its history
you can point at the one line that differs between the two files (the image, and FORGEJO__ versus GITEA__)

title: When Gitea or Forgejo Fits
text:
When Gitea or Forgejo Fits
After this page you can decide whether this shape is the forge for the job in front of you.

title: When Gitea or Forgejo Fits
text:
Choose it when
The requirement is Git hosting for a desk, a course, or a company that can name every user. You want issues and pull requests, you can live with CI as a webhook or a separate runner, and you would rather administer one data directory than a platform of services.
Forgejo is the default in this book for that job:

the steward is a non-profit, and the license from v9 on is GPL-3.0-or-later
15.0 is a long-term line (security support through 15 July 2027)
Codeberg is the same software, operated by someone else, when you do not want a server (chapter 29)

Gitea is the right lightweight forge when MIT is the constraint, or when a support contract with Gitea Ltd is the constraint. The operator experience is the sibling of Forgejo, not a different architecture.
Run it yourself when the repositories must stay on a machine you control. Use Codeberg when the code can live on a public community forge and you only need an account.

title: When Gitea or Forgejo Fits
text:
Choose something else when

You need merge trains, a built-in registry, dependency scanning, and GitLab CI on day one. That is chapter 24, and it is a larger machine.
Review must be a stack of patchsets with a Change-Id. That is Gerrit (chapter 27), not a pull-request UI with a different coat of paint.
The company standard is already GitHub or GitLab.com and the lock-in discussion in chapter 22 has been accepted. A second forge “for practice” is this lab. A second forge “for production beside the real one” is two metadata stores and one confused team.
You expect two nodes to share one SQLite file and call it high availability. Stop at the previous page and read chapter 37 before you draw that diagram.

title: When Gitea or Forgejo Fits
section: A decision you can write down
text:
A decision you can write down
small team, self-hosted, free-software forge  →  Forgejo 15 LTS
small team, MIT or a Gitea contract           →  Gitea 1.27
hosted community, no server to patch          →  Codeberg
CI and registry inside the installer          →  GitLab
Whichever line you pick, the developer workflow does not restart. desk-api is still a repository, the remote is still a URL, and force-push rules from chapter 11 still apply on main. Part V is what changes when you are the operator of that URL for other people: identity, branch protection, and backups. The binary will not do those for you.

title: Theory

Theory: workloadRef Lets a Rollout Adopt a Deployment
Migration is changing the controller that owns ReplicaSets without changing the pod spec. workloadRef points at an existing Deployment. StatefulSets often cannot follow this path.

title: Theory
text:
Invariants

Git (Argo) must stop managing the old Deployment’s replica field.
Aborts during migration need a rehearsed rollback.
Stateful identity (ordinals, PVCs) does not map to canary ReplicaSets cleanly.

Deployment  --workloadRef-->  Rollout takes over RS
Git desired: Rollout, not Deployment replicas

title: Theory
text:
What can break

Both Deployment and Rollout controllers racing on the same RS.

title: Theory
text:
Theory: One Loop from Commit to Careful Traffic
Git commit → forge CI → image digest in Git → Argo CD sync → Rollout steps → analysis → stable. That is the book’s end-to-end mental model.

title: Theory
text:
Invariants

Every stage is a name over content-addressed bytes (Git hash, image digest).
Humans change Git; controllers change clusters.
Larger environments add more clusters, ApplicationSets, and stricter analysis — not a different physics.

commit → CI → digest in Git → Argo → Rollout → traffic → stable

title: Theory
text:
What can break

A snowflake kubectl at any stage (breaks the loop).
